entries.title: A profile of Netflix's new Chief Content Officer Peter Rice, a former Fox and Disney executive, as sources say he may focus on revamping its film strategy (Alex Weprin/The Hollywood Reporter)
College students are increasingly pushing back against campus AI mandates, demanding opt-outs from AI-required assignments and an end to enterprise licenses (Dana Goldstein/New York Times)
Association for Advancing Automation: North American companies ordered ~11K robots in Q3 2026, up 25% YoY, as they seek to ease labor shortages in manufacturing (Christian Davies/Financial Times)
Alphabet Chief Investment Officer Ruth Porat says the company and its peers need to invest in jobs in places where data centers are being built amid backlash (Elena Eisenstadt/Bloomberg)
Sources expect Anthropic's IPO allocation for retail investors to fall below 20%; retail buyers have historically received 5% to 10% of shares in large IPOs (Financial Times)
Indian startup Sarvam, which is pursuing sovereign AI, is facing online backlash for offering Chinese open-weight models on its Token Factory inference service (Saritha Rai/Bloomberg)
Interviews with Anthropic employees reveal muted enthusiasm ahead of the largest IPO on record, as they debate the pace of frontier AI development (Jasmine Sun/New York Times)
Lenovo reports Q2 revenue up 48% YoY to $30.2B and a $640M net loss vs. $38M est., amid rising PC component costs; it posted its first operating loss since 2017 (Yuan Gao/Bloomberg)
A US congressional commission report says China's PLA is seeking advanced Nvidia chips for AI-enabled weapons, as domestic chips continue to lag US rivals (Jaspreet Singh/Reuters)
Sources: technical staff at several Chinese humanoid robot makers have been denied US visas ahead of CES, hampering their efforts to showcase their hardware (Nikkei Asia)
Internal posts show Meta employees raising concerns that Muse could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing users' private data (Katie Paul/Reuters)
Beijing-based MegaRobo, which uses robotics and AI to automate lab work for biotech research, raised ~$200M; it became a unicorn after raising $300M in 2022 (Bloomberg)
Kraken parent company Payward agrees to buy Tribe Capital, the VC firm formerly led by Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi; Tribe Capital has $2.7B in assets (CoinDesk)
Arizona's AG opens a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents" (David Thomas/Reuters)
Sources: Jeffrey Kessler, who oversees the Commerce Dept.'s BIS, pressured staff to expedite Nvidia H200 China sales despite red flags from other departments (The Information)
